questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words
[walk → jog → sprint] is analogous to [bothered → ________ → daunted].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.explanationEn: In '[walk -> jog -> sprint]', the words progress from mild to moderate to intense action. Similarly, 'bothered -> fazed -> daunted' shows increasing levels of disturbance, where 'fazed' means disturbed or disconcerted (whereas 'phased', 'phrased', and 'fused' do not fit the meaning).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Two wizards try to create a spell using all the four elements, water, air, fire, and
earth. For this, they decide to mix all these elements in all possible orders. They
also decide to work independently. After trying all possible combination of
elements, they conclude that the spell does not work.
How many attempts does each wizard make before coming to this conclusion,
independently?
questions.explanationEn: Mixing all 4 distinct elements in all possible orders corresponds to the number of permutations of 4 items, which is 4! = 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 24. Since the wizards work independently, each wizard makes 24 attempts.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In an engineering college of 10,000 students, 1,500 like neither their core branches
nor other branches. The number of students who like their core branches is 1/4th of
the number of students who like other branches. The number of students who like
both their core and other branches is 500.
The number of students who like their core branches is
questions.explanationEn: Out of 10,000 students, 10,000 - 1,500 = 8,500 like at least one branch. Let C and O be those liking core and other branches, with O = 4C and |C intersect O| = 500; by inclusion-exclusion, C + 4C - 500 = 8,500, giving 5C = 9,000 and C = 1,800.

questions.questionTextEn: In the sequence 6, 9, 14, x, 30, 41, a possible value of x is

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.
P:
This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and
heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the
contact zone.
Q: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological
event rather than as a static geological feature.
R: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large
quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and
making it better suited for life.
S:
Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate
collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
questions.explanationEn: Sentence S introduces the geological collision, P ('This fortuitous geological event...') describes its immediate result, R ('The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice...') describes the subsequent effect, and Q ('Thus...') draws the conclusion. This yields the coherent order SPRQ.

questions.questionTextEn:
A cube is to be cut into 8 pieces of equal size and shape. Here, each cut should be
straight and it should not stop till it reaches the other end of the cube.
The minimum number of such cuts required is
questions.explanationEn: Each straight planar cut along one of the three orthogonal axes (length, width, height) doubles the number of pieces. Making 1 cut along each of the 3 perpendicular mid-planes produces 2 * 2 * 2 = 8 equal smaller cubes, so 3 cuts suffice.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a computer with a 4 MHz processor. Its DMA controller can transfer
8 bytes in 1 cycle from a device to main memory through cycle stealing at regular
intervals. Which one of the following is the data transfer rate (in bits per second) of
the DMA controller if 1% of the processor cycles are used for DMA?
questions.explanationEn: At 4 MHz, 1% of cycles gives 0.01 * 4 * 10^6 = 40,000 DMA cycles per second. Transferring 8 bytes (64 bits) per cycle yields a transfer rate of 40,000 * 64 = 2,560,000 bits/sec.

Consider the statement: “Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than

Which one of the following is the CORRECT representation of the above statement

questions.explanationEn: 'When q (student scores > 50% marks), not p (fail grade cannot be given)' translates directly to the implication q -> not p.

Choose the largest floating-point number among the following options.

questions.explanationEn: In IEEE 754 single precision, an all-1s exponent (1111 1111) represents Infinity or NaN rather than a finite floating-point number (ruling out C). questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let T(n) be the recurrence relation defined as follows:
T(0) = 1,
T(1) = 2, and
T(n) = 5T(n−1) −6T(n−2) for n≥2
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: The characteristic equation r^2 - 5r + 6 = 0 has roots r = 2 and r = 3, so T(n) = c1 * 2^n + c2 * 3^n. Using T(0) = c1 + c2 = 1 and T(1) = 2*c1 + 3*c2 = 2 gives c1 = 1 and c2 = 0, so T(n) = 2^n = Theta(2^n).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let A be the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph G. Suppose A is its own
inverse. Which one of the following statements is always TRUE?
optionsEn: There is no such graph G
questions.explanationEn: For an undirected simple graph, A is symmetric and has 0s on the diagonal. If A^(-1) = A, then A^2 = I, meaning every vertex i has degree (A^2)_ii = 1 and no two distinct vertices share a common neighbor; thus every vertex has degree 1, so G is a perfect matching (disjoint union of edges).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
When six unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously, the probability of getting all
distinct numbers (i.e., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6) is
questions.explanationEn: There are 6^6 total outcomes and 6! outcomes with all distinct numbers. The probability is 6! / 6^6 = 720 / 46656 = 5 / 324.

are reflected on disk. This property is called

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In the context of owner and weak entity sets in the ER (Entity-Relationship) data
model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?
optionsEn: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
The owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Both weak and owner entity sets MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Neither weak entity set nor owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
questions.explanationEn: In an ER model, a weak entity depends on an identifying owner entity for its existence and primary key, so every weak entity instance must be associated with an owner entity—meaning the weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.topicTag: Computer Networks — Data Link & Network Layer
questions.questionTextEn:
Node X has a TCP connection open to node Y. The packets from X to Y go through
an intermediate IP router R. Ethernet switch S is the first switch on the network path
between X and R. Consider a packet sent from X to Y over this connection.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the destination IP and MAC
addresses on this packet at the time it leaves X?
optionsEn: The destination IP address is the IP address of R
The destination IP address is the IP address of Y
The destination MAC address is the MAC address of S
The destination MAC address is the MAC address of Y
questions.explanationEn: As the IP packet leaves X toward Y via intermediate router R, the Layer-3 destination IP address is the final destination Y (B is true). Because Ethernet switch S is a transparent Layer-2 device, the Layer-2 destination MAC address on the frame is the MAC address of the next-hop router R (not S or Y), making only (B) true.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following tasks is/are the responsibility/responsibilities of the memory
management unit (MMU) in a system with paging-based memory management?
optionsEn: Allocate a new page table for a newly created process
Translate a virtual address to a physical address using the page table
Raise a trap when a virtual address is not found in the page table
Raise a trap when a process tries to write to a page marked with read-only permission in the page table
questions.explanationEn: The MMU performs hardware virtual-to-physical address translation using page tables/TLB (B) and raises page-fault traps on missing/invalid translations (C) or protection traps on permission violations like writing a read-only page (D). Allocating a page table for a new process is handled by the OS kernel, not the MMU.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a process P running on a CPU. Which one or more of the following events
will always trigger a context switch by the OS that results in process P moving to a
non-running state (e.g., ready, blocked)?
optionsEn: P makes a blocking system call to read a block of data from the disk
P tries to access a page that is in the swap space, triggering a page fault
An interrupt is raised by the disk to deliver data requested by some other process
A timer interrupt is raised by the hardware
questions.explanationEn: A blocking disk I/O system call (A) and a page fault to swap space (B) both block process P until I/O completes, forcing the OS to switch P out of running state. A timer interrupt or disk completion interrupt for another process invokes an ISR, but the scheduler may resume P without moving P to a non-running state.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following file organizations is/are I/O efficient for the scan operation
in DBMS?
questions.explanationEn: Scanning an entire relation reads pages sequentially in Sorted (A) or Heap (B) file organizations, minimizing random disk seeks. Unclustered tree or hash indexes store pointers to records scattered randomly across data pages, causing excessive random I/O during full scans.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements about the Two Phase Locking (2PL) protocol
is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: With 2PL, a transaction always locks the data item being read or written just before every operation and always releases the lock just after the operation
With 2PL, once a lock is released on any data item inside a transaction, no more locks on any data item can be obtained inside that transaction
questions.explanationEn: Two-Phase Locking guarantees conflict serializability (A) because transactions follow a growing phase then a shrinking phase where no new locks can be acquired after releasing any lock (C), though deadlocks remain possible (D). Option (B) describes immediate acquire-release per operation rather than 2PL.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the datagram
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU
The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram
The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the path from the source to the destination
questions.explanationEn: In IPv4, any intermediate router (as well as the source) fragments a datagram if its size exceeds the outgoing link's MTU and DF=0 (B). Fragments are reassembled only at the final destination host (C), not at intermediate routers.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
optionsEn: An attribute grammar is a syntax-directed definition (SDD) in which the functions in the semantic rules have no side effects
The attributes in a L-attributed definition cannot always be evaluated in a depth- first order
Synthesized attributes can be evaluated by a bottom-up parser as the input is parsed
All L-attributed definitions based on LR(1) grammar can be evaluated using a bottom-up parsing strategy
questions.explanationEn: By definition, L-attributed SDDs can always be evaluated in a single depth-first (left-to-right) traversal (so B is FALSE). Moreover, not all L-attributed SDDs on LR(1) grammars can be evaluated during bottom-up LR parsing—only a restricted subclass (e.g., S-attributed or those convertible via marker non-terminals) can (so D is FALSE). Statements A and C are true.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: For a Boolean variable x, which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
questions.explanationEn: In Boolean algebra, x + 1 = 1 (not x, so B is FALSE) and x . x = x (not 0, so C is FALSE). Identities x . 1 = x (A) and x + x' = 1 (D) are always true.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An instruction format has the following structure:
Instruction Number: Opcode destination reg, source reg-1, source reg-2
Consider the following sequence of instructions to be executed in a pipelined
processor:
I1: DIV R3, R1, R2
I2: SUB R5, R3, R4
I3: ADD R3, R5, R6
I4: MUL R7, R3, R8
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I1 and I2
There is a WAR dependency on R3 between I1 and I3
There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I2 and I3
There is a WAW dependency on R3 between I3 and I4
questions.explanationEn: I1 writes R3 and I2 reads R3, creating a Read-After-Write (RAW) dependency on R3 between I1 and I2 (A). Between I1 and I3, both write R3 (WAW, not WAR); between I2 and I3, the RAW dependency is on R5 (not R3); and between I3 and I4, I3 writes R3 and I4 reads R3 (RAW, not WAW).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router
before it forwards the IP packet?
questions.explanationEn: Every IP router decrements the Time to Live (TTL) field by 1 before forwarding (C), which changes the IP header and therefore requires recomputing the Header Checksum (D). Source IP and Protocol remain unchanged (unless NAT is used).

Ordering {1, 2, 3} with 1 < 2 and 3 < 2 allows two orders: (1, 3, 2) and (3, 1, 2). In (1, 3, 2), 4 can go after 3 (2 positions: 1,3,4,2 or 1,3,2,4); in (3, 1, 2), 4 can go anywhere after 3 (3 positions: 3,4,1,2; 3,1,4,2; 3,1,2,4), giving 2 + 3 = 5 total orders.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let Abe an array containing integer values. The distance of A is defined as the
minimum number of elements in A that must be replaced with another integer so
that the resulting array is sorted in non-decreasing order. The distance of the array
[2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6] is ___________
questions.explanationEn: Keeping the longest non-decreasing subsequence (LNDS) of A = [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6] fixed and replacing all other elements minimizes replacements. An LNDS is [2, 3, 4, 6] of length 4 (out of 7 elements), so at least 7 - 4 = 3 elements must be replaced.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a single processor system with four processes A, B, C, and D, represented
as given below, where for each process the first value is its arrival time, and the
second value is its CPU burst time.
A (0, 10), B (2, 6), C (4, 3), and D (6, 7).
Which one of the following options gives the average waiting times when
preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) and Non-Preemptive Shortest
Job First (NP-SJF) CPU scheduling algorithms are applied to the processes?
questions.explanationEn: Under SRTF: A runs 0–2 (rem 8), B runs 2–4 (rem 4), C runs 4–7 (finishes at 7, WT=0), B runs 7–11 (finishes at 11, WT=3), D runs 11–18 (finishes at 18, WT=5), A runs 18–26 (finishes at 26, WT=16), giving avg WT = (16+3+0+5)/4 = 6. Under NP-SJF: A runs 0–10 (WT=0), C runs 10–13 (WT=6), B runs 13–19 (WT=11), D runs 19–26 (WT=13), giving avg WT = (0+6+11+13)/4 = 7.5.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the following CIDR prefixes exactly represents the range of
IP addresses 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255?
questions.explanationEn: The range 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255 spans two consecutive /24 blocks (512 addresses), where the third octet is 2 (00000010) and 3 (00000011). These share the first 7 bits of the third octet (0000001x), giving the /23 prefix 10.12.2.0/23.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
You are given a set V of distinct integers. A binary search tree T is created by
inserting all elements of V one by one, starting with an empty tree. The tree T
follows the convention that, at each node, all values stored in the left subtree of the
node are smaller than the value stored at the node. You are not aware of the sequence
in which these values were inserted into T, and you do not have access to T.
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
optionsEn: Inorder traversal of T can be determined from V
Root node of T can be determined from V
Preorder traversal of T can be determined from V
Postorder traversal of T can be determined from V
questions.explanationEn: The inorder traversal of any BST visits its keys in strictly sorted (ascending) order. Because the set V of distinct integers uniquely determines its sorted order, the inorder traversal is uniquely determined from V, whereas the root, preorder, and postorder depend on insertion order.

questions.explanationEn: Triple (1) loads array element s[i] via operator '=[]' with operands s and i. Triple (3) multiplies triple (0) (p + r) by triple (2) (-s[i]), giving '* (0) (2)'. Triple (6) addresses l-value x[i] via '[]=' with operands x and i, matching Option (A).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let x and y be random variables, not necessarily independent, that take real values
in the interval [0,1]. Let z= xy and let the mean values of x, y, z be x̅, y̅, z̅,
respectively. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: Since x and y take values in [0, 1], we always have 0 <= y <= 1 and x >= 0, which implies xy <= x everywhere. Taking expectations on both sides gives E[z] = E[xy] <= E[x], i.e., z_bar <= x_bar.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The relation schema, Person(pid,city), describes the city of residence for
every person uniquely identified by pid. The following relational algebra operators
are available: selection, projection, cross product, and rename.
To find the list of cities where at least 3 persons reside, using the above operators,
the minimum number of cross product operations that must be used is
questions.explanationEn: To find cities with at least 3 distinct persons (p1, p2, p3 with the same city and distinct pids p1 != p2, p2 != p3, p1 != p3), we must join Person with itself three times (Person x Person x Person), which requires a minimum of 2 cross product operations.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
optionsEn: T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 runs next and prints 2
T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 runs next and prints 2
T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 does not print anything (deadlock)
T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 does not print anything (deadlock)
questions.explanationEn: If T2 runs first, wait(s1) succeeds, x becomes 1, prints 1, signal(s2) sets s2=1, signal(s1) sets s1=1; then T1 acquires s1, increments x to 2, prints 2, consumes s2, and releases s1 (B). If T1 runs first, wait(s1) succeeds, x becomes 1, prints 1, and T1 blocks on wait(s2) while holding s1; T2 then blocks on wait(s1), causing deadlock (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let A be an n× n matrix over the set of all real numbers R. Let B be a matrix
obtained from A by swapping two rows. Which of the following statements is/are
TRUE?
optionsEn: The determinant of B is the negative of the determinant of A
If A is invertible, then B is also invertible
If Ais symmetric, then B is also symmetric
If the trace of A is zero, then the trace of Bis also zero
questions.explanationEn: Swapping two rows of a square matrix negates its determinant (det(B) = -det(A), A), and since det(B) != 0 iff det(A) != 0, B is invertible whenever A is (B). Symmetry and zero trace are not preserved under arbitrary row swaps (C and D are false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let S1 and S2 be two stacks. S1 has capacity of 4 elements. S2 has capacity of
2 elements. S1 already has 4 elements: 100, 200, 300, and 400, whereas S2 is
empty, as shown below.
Only the following three operations are available:
400 (Top)
300
200
100
Stack S1
Stack S2
PushToS2: Pop the top element from S1 and push it on S2.
PushToS1: Pop the top element from S2 and push it on S1.
GenerateOutput: Pop the top element from S1 and output it to the
user.
Note that the pop operation is not allowed on an empty stack and the push operation
is not allowed on a full stack.
Which of the following output sequences can be generated by using the above
operations?
questions.explanationEn: Because S2 holds at most 2 items, (B) 200, 300, 400, 100 succeeds by pushing 400 and 300 to S2, outputting 200, returning 300 then 400 to S1 to output them, and outputting 100. Similarly (C) and (D) require at most 1 item in S2 at a time, whereas (A) 100, 200, 400, 300 requires pushing 400, 300, and 200 (3 items) onto S2 before outputting 100, exceeding S2's capacity.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider 4-variable functions f1, f2, f3, f4 expressed in sum-of-minterms form as
given below.
f1 = ∑(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13)
f2 = ∑(1,3,5,7,11,13, 15)
f3 = ∑(0,1,4,11)
f4 = ∑(0,2,6,13)
With respect to the circuit given above, which of the following options is/are
CORRECT?
questions.explanationEn: Evaluating the combinational logic circuit built from f1, f2, f3, f4 (refer to the official circuit diagram) yields minterms {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, which equals Sigma(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7) (C) and equivalently maxterms Pi(8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15) (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G be an undirected connected graph in which every edge has a positive integer
weight. Suppose that every spanning tree in G has even weight. Which of the
following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph G ?
optionsEn: All edges in G have even weight
All edges in G have even weight OR all edges in G have odd weight
In each cycle C in G, all edges in C have even weight
In each cycle C in G, either all edges in C have even weight OR all edges in C have odd weight
questions.explanationEn: Swapping any two edges in the same cycle C preserves whether a subgraph is a spanning tree, so all edges in C must share the same weight parity for every spanning tree to have even weight. Thus in every cycle C, either all edges have even weight or all edges have odd weight (D); a triangle of three odd-weight edges shows A, B, and C need not hold.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a context-free grammar G with the following 3 rules.
S→aS, S→aSbS, S→c
Let w∈L(G). Let na(w), nb(w), nc(w)denote the number of times a, b, c
occur in w, respectively. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: Every production increases the count of c by 1 only at S -> c and b by 1 only at S -> aSbS (which adds one S), so by induction n_c(w) = n_b(w) + 1 (C). Also each S -> aSbS adds one 'a' and one extra 'c' (via the second S), while S -> c gives n_a=0, n_c=1, so n_a(w) >= n_c(w) - 1 > n_c(w) - 2 (B).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM,
average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.
A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming
average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal
places) to read the entire file from the disk is _________
questions.explanationEn: At 6000 RPM (100 RPS), one rotation takes 10 ms, so average rotational latency is 5 ms and 1-sector transfer time is 10/500 = 0.02 ms. Each of the 3000 randomly placed sectors takes 5 ms (seek) + 5 ms (rotational latency) + 0.02 ms (transfer) = 10.02 ms, totaling 3000 * 10.02 ms = 30.06 seconds (in 29.50 to 30.50).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window
of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet
loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip
Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the
third RTT will be _________
questions.explanationEn: Upon timeout at cwnd = 12 MSS, ssthresh becomes 12/2 = 6 MSS and cwnd resets to 1 MSS (1st RTT after loss). After all segments in RTT 1 are ACKed, cwnd doubles to 2 MSS (2nd RTT), and after RTT 2 is ACKed, cwnd doubles to 4 MSS (3rd RTT).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of 108 bits/sec and a
maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal
in the medium is 2×108 meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required
for collision detection is _________
questions.explanationEn: For CSMA/CD collision detection, transmission time must be at least 2 * T_prop. Here 2 * T_prop = 2 * (500 m) / (2 * 10^8 m/s) = 5 * 10^(-6) s, so minimum frame size = (10^8 bits/s) * (5 * 10^(-6) s) = 500 bits.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A functional dependency F:X→Y is termed as a useful functional dependency if
and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:
• X is not the empty set.
• Y is not the empty set.
• Intersection of X and Y is the empty set.
For a relation R with 4 attributes, the total number of possible useful functional
dependencies is ________
questions.explanationEn: For 4 attributes, each attribute can go into X, into Y, or into neither (3^4 = 81 total disjoint pairs). Subtracting pairs with X = empty (2^4 = 16) and pairs with Y = empty (2^4 = 16), and adding back X = Y = empty (counted twice, 1), gives 81 - 16 - 16 + 1 = 50 useful FDs.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A processor with 16 general purpose registers uses a 32-bit instruction format. The
instruction format consists of an opcode field, an addressing mode field, two register
operand fields, and a 16-bit scalar field. If 8 addressing modes are to be supported,
the maximum number of unique opcodes possible for every addressing mode
is _________
questions.explanationEn: With 16 registers, each register field needs 4 bits (2 * 4 = 8 bits), 8 addressing modes need 3 bits, and the scalar field uses 16 bits. This leaves 32 - (8 + 3 + 16) = 5 bits for the opcode, supporting up to 2^5 = 32 unique opcodes.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A non-pipelined instruction execution unit operating at 2 GHz takes an average of
6 cycles to execute an instruction of a program P. The unit is then redesigned to
operate on a 5-stage pipeline at 2 GHz. Assume that the ideal throughput of the
pipelined unit is 1 instruction per cycle. In the execution of program P,
20% instructions incur an average of 2 cycles stall due to data hazards and
20% instructions incur an average of 3 cycles stall due to control hazards. The
speedup (rounded off to one decimal place) obtained by the pipelined design over
the non-pipelined design is _________
questions.explanationEn: Both designs run at 2 GHz, so speedup = CPI_nonpipelined / CPI_pipelined. Here CPI_nonpipelined = 6, and CPI_pipelined = 1 + 0.20*2 + 0.20*3 = 1 + 0.4 + 0.6 = 2.0, giving speedup = 6 / 2.0 = 3.0 (in 2.9 to 3.1).

The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a
proper colouring of the graph. The chromatic number of the following graph
is _________
questions.explanationEn: Inspecting the graph in the official question paper shows it contains at least one edge and no odd cycles (it is bipartite). Hence its chromatic number is 2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A processor uses a 32-bit instruction format and supports byte-addressable memory
access. The ISA of the processor has 150 distinct instructions. The instructions are
equally divided into two types, namely R-type and I-type, whose formats are shown
below.
R-type Instruction Format:
OPCODE UNUSED DST Register
SRC Register1
SRC Register 2
I-type Instruction Format:
OPCODE DST Register SRC Register # Immediate value/address
In the OPCODE, 1 bit is used to distinguish between I-type and R-type instructions
and the remaining bits indicate the operation. The processor has 50 architectural
registers, and all register fields in the instructions are of equal size.
Let X be the number of bits used to encode the UNUSED field, Y be the number
of bits used to encode the OPCODE field, and Z be the number of bits used to
encode the immediate value/address field. The value of X+ 2Y+ Z is ________
questions.explanationEn: There are 75 R-type and 75 I-type instructions; distinguishing R/I takes 1 bit and identifying 75 operations within a type needs ceil(log2(75)) = 7 bits, so Y = 1 + 7 = 8 bits. With 50 registers, each register field needs ceil(log2(50)) = 6 bits. In 32-bit R-type (OPCODE + UNUSED + 3 regs): X = 32 - (8 + 18) = 6; in I-type (OPCODE + 2 regs + imm): Z = 32 - (8 + 12) = 12, giving X + 2Y + Z = 6 + 16 + 12 = 34.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let L1 be the language represented by the regular expression b∗ab∗(ab∗ab∗)∗
and L2 = {w∈(a+ b)∗||w| ≤4}, where |w| denotes the length of string
w. The number of strings in L2 which are also in L1 is ___________
questions.explanationEn: L1 = b*ab*(ab*ab*)* is the set of all strings over {a, b} containing an ODD number of a's. Among strings in L2 of length <= 4: for length 1 (1 string), length 2 (2 strings), length 3 (4 strings), and length 4 (8 strings)—in general, half of the 2^k strings of length k >= 1 have an odd number of a's—so 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 strings.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let Zn be the group of integers {0, 1, 2, ... , n−1} with addition modulo n as the
group operation. The number of elements in the group Z2 × Z3 × Z4 that are their
own inverses is ________
questions.explanationEn: An element (x, y, z) in Z2 x Z3 x Z4 is its own inverse iff 2x = 0 (mod 2), 2y = 0 (mod 3), and 2z = 0 (mod 4). That gives x in {0, 1} (2 choices), y in {0} (1 choice), and z in {0, 2} (2 choices), totaling 2 * 1 * 2 = 4 elements.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a 32-bit system with 4 KB page size and page table entries of size 4 bytes
each. Assume 1 KB = 210 bytes. The OS uses a 2-level page table for memory
management, with the page table containing an outer page directory and an inner
page table. The OS allocates a page for the outer page directory upon process
creation. The OS uses demand paging when allocating memory for the inner page
table, i.e., a page of the inner page table is allocated only if it contains at least one
valid page table entry.
An active process in this system accesses 2000 unique pages during its execution,
and none of the pages are swapped out to disk. After it completes the page accesses,
let X denote the minimum and Y denote the maximum number of pages across the
two levels of the page table of the process.
The value of X+Y is ________
questions.explanationEn: Each 4 KB page holds 4096 / 4 = 1024 PTEs, so 1 outer page directory (always allocated) + inner page tables are used. Minimum pages X occurs when all 2000 PTEs are packed into ceil(2000 / 1024) = 2 inner pages, giving X = 1 + 2 = 3; maximum pages Y occurs when the 2000 accessed pages fall into 1024 distinct outer entries (since the outer directory has 1024 entries), using 1024 inner pages and Y = 1 + 1024 = 1025. Thus X + Y = 3 + 1025 = 1028.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2024 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following augmented grammar, which is to be parsed with a SLR
parser. The set of terminals is {a,b,c,d,#,@}
S′ →S
S→SS|Aa|bAc|Bc|bBa
A→d#
B→@
Let I0 = CLOSURE({S′ →• S}). The number of items in the set GOTO(I0, S)
is ___________
questions.explanationEn: Advancing the dot over S from I0 = CLOSURE({S' -> .S}) produces the 2 kernel items {S' -> S., S -> S.S}. Taking CLOSURE adds the 7 items {S -> .SS, S -> .Aa, S -> .bAc, S -> .Bc, S -> .bBa, A -> .d#, B -> .@}, yielding 2 + 7 = 9 LR(0) items.
